iut_type: End Product — A2DP profile (audio system / AVN)
customer_question: N/A — internal report review. Two issues flagged: (1) test case A2DP/SNK/SYN/[ID] is present in the test plan but was not executed; (2) profile version was written as X.Y (two digits) instead of X.Y.Z (three digits).
question_variants: Is it acceptable to omit a test case from the A2DP test without marking it as excluded?
Does the A2DP profile version need a third digit (Z term) in the report?
actual_issue: During internal report review for an AlpsAlpine 19AVN A2DP profile test, two compliance issues were identified: (1) A2DP/SNK/SYN/[ID] test case appeared in the test plan but no test result was recorded — the case was simply skipped without documentation; (2) the A2DP profile version was reported as X.Y (e.g., 1.3) rather than the required three-digit format X.Y.Z (e.g., 1.3.0).
plain_english_explanation: The report had two formatting/completeness issues. First, a test case was listed in the plan but never run — you can't just leave a gap; either run it or explicitly mark it as excluded with a reason. Second, Bluetooth profile versions require three digits (e.g., 1.3.0), not two (1.3).
consultant_answer: Both issues must be corrected before the report is approved: (1) the A2DP/SNK/SYN test case must either be executed or formally marked as excluded in the test plan with justification; (2) the profile version must be expressed in X.Y.Z format (three-digit, including the patch/minor version Z term).
decision_logic: SIG profile reports must account for all test cases in the test plan. Unexecuted cases without documented exclusion constitute a gap that will fail review. Profile version notation requires the full three-digit format per SIG convention.
final_recommendation: Review all test plans before submitting reports to confirm every listed test case has either a result or an explicit exclusion reason. Always write profile versions in X.Y.Z format.
risk_if_done_wrong: Submitting a report with unaccounted test cases or incorrect version notation will cause review rejection and require corrections and resubmission, adding delay.
